score.note: Two 080bbb0c transfer passes recovered the complete state machine and cut the candidate-show wrong-instruction residual by 54.0%, from 876 to 403. Repeated operand loads, a full-width animation-frame carrier, a loop-invariant part-flag carrier, reference-shaped record cursors, exact access width, and declaration lifetime were all material; the retained assembly remains authoritative.

rejected.result: the trailing word reached the exact frame extent but regressed to 420 wrong instructions; the leading word also aligned records at sp+12 and selection at sp+28 but regressed to 416, because the runtime carrier remained at sp+4 instead of the reference sp+8

rejected.result: this moved records and selection to the reference stack offsets and grew the candidate to 1868 bytes, only 8 bytes short of the reference, but still scored 412 wrong instructions and 691 differing halfwords; it was rejected in favor of the smaller readable 410-row baseline

rejected.shape: bounded compiler pass sweep after the stack audit
rejected.result: -fno-gcse was the sole material diagnostic at 371 wrong instructions (from 410). Pairing it with -fno-schedule-insns2, -fno-cse-follow-jumps, -fno-cse-skip-blocks, -fno-regmove, -fno-rerun-cse-after-loop, or -fno-expensive-optimizations scored 424, 415, 543, 373, 459, and 616 respectively. The flag is not an approved owner route and therefore was not adopted; it isolates GCSE/PRE shaping as the next source-level axis.

rejected.shape: full-width frame plus loop-invariant part flag and explicit record-gather loop
rejected.result: this fixed-route source improvement removes the byte truncation absent from the reference, hoists the 0xff part flag into the reference-shaped high-register carrier, and stores gathered records only after a successful lookup. It improves the readable routed candidate from 1852/687/410 to 1868/687/403. Re-running -fno-gcse on the improved source gives 1856/683/382, confirming that the source change absorbs part of the earlier PRE signal without relying on a nonstandard route.

rejected.shape: third-pass dispatcher carrier and phase-5 lifetime audit
rejected.result: the reference keeps the loaded event index in r5 and copies it to r6 for dispatch, but a distinct readable dispatch_index local is coalesced by the fixed compiler and is byte-neutral. Moving phase-5 viewport/display carriers into the narrow phase scope is also byte-neutral; reversing the tile/scroll expression order regresses to 413 wrong instructions. register hints are ignored. The remaining dispatcher and phase-5 distance is allocation/literal placement rather than a missing switch case, width conversion, or observable source lifetime, so none of these spellings replaced the 403-row best source.

notes: The relocation-aware comparison used the retained EN assembly object as an exact locator; it proves shared machine-code core, not recovered C source.
The JA-to-EN owner shift is +0x9000, exactly matching 080b2b0c to 080bbb0c.
The phase-local record and selection workspace is deliberately explicit because its stack addresses are observable across calls.
No external source, git history, compiler modification, copied instruction bytes, fixed-register variables, barriers, or inline assembly was used.
